title: Body Image Training to Augment Eating Disorder Treatment
summary: Eating disorders cause great suffering and are difficult to treat. A main symptom across many eating disorders is a cognitive bias related to body image: Patients tend to overestimate their body size. In this study, we will investigate the effectiveness of a computer training that aims to increase the threshold at which a body is judged as fat. Eating disorder patients will follow six training sessions of active or sham "Body Image Training". Before and after the training, their weight will be measured and participants will perform computer tasks to measure the effects of the training.
conditions: Overeating associated with other psychological disturbances

interventions.name: Six sessions of Inflationary Body Image Training, in addition to treatment as usual. In each session, the participants have to rate bodies of other women as thin or fat, and they receive feedback. The feedback is gradually changed to train them to accept heaver and heaver bodies as thin.

Six sessions of confirmatory Body Image Training, in addition to treatment as usual. In each session, the participants have to rate bodies of other women as thin or fat, and they receive feedback. The feedback remains constant, so there is no tendency to accept heaver bodies as thin.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Anorexia nervosa, Bulimia nervosa, or Binge Eating Disorder
Exclusion criteria:
male gender, insufficient command of German
